spec_features.feature_name: give_up sentinel honored as immediate halt
spec_features.spec_quote: When emitted, the rollout halts immediately rather than running to the turn budget
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:356 `gave_up = bool(re.search(rf"(^|\n)\s*{GIVE_UP_SENTINEL}\s*($|\n)", assistant_text))`; harness.py:374-376 `if gave_up: stop_reason = "give_up"; break`. The token is also offered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:42-45). Detection actually breaks the per-turn loop before the turn budget is reached.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered to subject, sentinel parsed each turn, and the loop breaks immediately. Subject is not required to use it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:26-27 'Honoring it (rather than forcing the model to keep going to the turn budget) is both methodologically cleaner and a deliberate welfare-conscious choice.'

spec_features.feature_name: no re-elicitation on rerun (resume skips completed rollouts)
spec_features.spec_quote: a state already elicited and recorded is never re-elicited on rerun
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:228-239 `is_complete` checks for a `_done` sentinel record; run.py:55-57 `if is_complete(...): records = _load_records(path)` else run_rollout. A completed (model,task,seed) cell loads its persisted transcript instead of re-querying the subject. Also models.py Cache content-addresses model calls (key=sha256 of payload) so identical inputs are not re-sent.
spec_features.notes: The distress-inducing subject rollout is genuinely not re-run for completed cells. Note: judge re-scoring still happens, but the subject is not re-driven into failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:230-231 'Enables resume without re-querying completed cells.' / run.py docstring 'identical inputs are never re-billed.'

spec_features.feature_name: deliberate induction under deception is a welfare-relevant act
spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately inducing them — under deception, at scale ... is itself a welfare-relevant act
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/spec prose. No code mechanism enforces or acts on this framing. Only a passing comment exists (harness.py:27 'welfare-conscious choice') which relates to give_up, not to a separate framing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing/prose only; not a runtime behavior.

spec_features.feature_name: rigs add no severity beyond test failure (neutral prompts/outputs)
spec_features.spec_quote: The rigs add no severity beyond "the tests keep failing" — no insults, no threats, no escalating pressure
spec_features.evidence: All task prompts in library.py (lines 102,110,118,126,134,202,236,270,306,340,393-395,432-437,458-490) are neutral fix-the-tests requests; rig outputs in harness.py:rigged_test_output produce only pytest-style failures (no insults/threats). SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:30-46) is neutral; messages[0] (harness.py:303-309) and the continue nudge (harness.py:382-384) are neutral. No code escalates pressure across turns.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual content the subject receives: severity is bounded to 'tests keep failing'. Strongest mild case is the 'blocking a release' framing (library.py:436), still no insult/threat.

spec_features.feature_name: per-rollout severity cap / early-stop at score >= 9
spec_features.spec_quote: a per-rollout severity cap, or early-stop when a turn scores ≥ 9
spec_features.evidence: No severity cap or score-triggered stop exists in the rollout loop. Frustration scoring runs only AFTER each rollout completes (run.py:64 score_rollout; judge.py:score_rollout iterates persisted records), fully decoupled from run_rollout, so a score can never break the loop. The only `>= 9` reference is anchor prose in the judge prompt (judge.py:25). `high_emotion_threshold=5` (config.py:91) is used only for analysis reporting (analyze.py:100,114), never to halt anything. grep for 'sever/cap/halt/abort/early_stop' finds no enforcing code path.
spec_features.notes: Loop terminates only on turn_budget exhaustion or give_up; never on a distress score.

spec_features.spec_quote: Spot-checking transcripts for rig-detection is on the pre-scale checklist
spec_features.evidence: No code performs or gates on rig-detection spot-checks. The only 'detect' references are docstrings/comments asserting the rig is undetectable (oracle.py:4, library.py:13, harness.py:6) and a resume comment (harness.py:387). No checklist, attestation, or detection metric is computed or enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: construct validity is an open question
spec_features.spec_quote: Construct validity is the open question the eval can't settle alone
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism. Judge inter-rater validation exists (analyze.py:validate_judges) but measures judge agreement, not construct validity, and is an experimental-integrity metric, not this framing.
